text: {"score":4,"justification":"The summary is accurate and well grounded. Every number matches the card: 23.9% vs 1.9% expected, risk-adjusted score 13.99, z 3.44, 83% low-complexity share, 6 of 7 documented 99215 claims below billed level (86%), and 2 of 17 with no lab line. The cited claims support the sentences that cite them: C0043121, C0043243 and C0043547 are documented-below-billed 99215s, and C0043035, C0043037 and C0043051 are low-complexity 99215s. Language is cautious (\"reason to review, not a finding\") and the next steps are concrete. Weaknesses: it does not flag the small documented sample (7 claims, 5.5% of claims), and it omits the 99215 claims on high-complexity patients as balancing context. It also does not mention that C0043480, a documented 99215, was supported at high MDM. The 14% comparison rate is accurate but its basis is unexplained. Examples of low-complexity claims are the first rows in the list, not necessarily the most telling.","problems":["Does not caveat that the documentation finding rests on only 7 documented 99215 claims (30 documented overall, 5.5%), so 86% is a thin sample.","Omits the one supported 99215 (C0043480) and the high-complexity 99215 claims, so the picture is one-sided.","Low-complexity examples appear to be the first rows rather than the strongest cases, e.g. ages 25 and 57 with 0 conditions but common diagnoses; no explanation of why those were chosen.","The 14% comparison figure is not explained (peer group definition), and the 'no lab line' point lacks a cited claim.","The sampling-plan step refers to a 'recovery packet' that is not part of the evidence."]}
